findings.title: Sweep inventory contradicts the design's own exclusions: most listed sites are `SliceStatus`-typed or raw-frontmatter, not `NormalizedStatus`-typed
findings.description:
The Technical Scope table claims every included site "assigns or compares a `NormalizedStatus` value as a bare string literal," and TD-3 (slice doc:104-110) explicitly rules `SliceStatus.status` out of scope because conflating it with `NormalizedStatus` "implies the two unions are related, which they aren't." The code shows the table includes exactly those excluded sites:

- **All 3 `WorkflowNavigator.ts` sites are `SliceStatus`-typed.** Lines 312 and 345 compare `slice.status === 'complete'` where `slice` is declared `Promise<SliceStatus>` (WorkflowNavigator.ts:525, 532); line 588 assigns `status: 'complete'` into a `SliceStatus`. These are the `SliceStatus.status` union TD-3 says to "leave untouched," yet lines 36, 75, and migration step 4 (line 90) sweep them.
- **Most of `ConsistencyChecker.ts`'s 36 claimed sites are raw-frontmatter strings, not `NormalizedStatus`.** `planStatus` (lines 715, 717, 733, 962, 967, 983) and `archStatus` (811, 814, 830, 884-885) are `frontmatter.data.status.toLowerCase()` — type `string` from `FrontmatterData`. `fmStatus` sites (351, 357, 373, 463, 469, 485, 513) are likewise raw; line 513 even performs `.replace(/_/g, '-')` — an ad-hoc raw-token-to-normalized-spelling conversion, i.e., precisely the vocabulary mixing TD-2 warns against. Only ~6 sites (`taskResult.inferredStatus` comparisons at 286, 325, 352, 392, 519, 535) are genuinely `NormalizedStatus`-typed.
- **~12 `detail: { value: 'complete' | 'in-progress' }` sites (368, 384, 403, 480, 546, 728, 744, 825, 841, 914, 978, 994) are write-path values, not in-memory comparisons.** They flow through `updateFrontmatterField` (ConsistencyChecker.ts:213-214) into user documents' frontmatter — the raw frontmatter vocabulary TD-2 (slice doc:97-102) declares "intentionally distinct" from `STATUS`. The scope table counts them as sweepable `NormalizedStatus` sites without ever identifying them as frontmatter writes. (Side observation worth checking separately: `VALID_STATUSES` contains `'complete'` but not `'in-progress'`, so a checker fix writing `'in-progress'` appears to emit an out-of-vocabulary token — pre-existing, but it underlines that these sites live in the raw vocabulary.)

The genuinely in-scope inventory is ~22 occurrences (14 `STATUS_MAP` values, 4 `taskFileParser` assignments, 4 `slicePlanParser` ternaries, plus the `types.ts:44` retype), not "~65 across 6 files." As written, the design is unactionable: an implementer following the table violates TD-3 and TD-2's rationale; an implementer honoring TD-3 cannot fill the table or meet the success criteria. The sites that *are* correctly scoped (statusNormalizer values, taskFileParser, slicePlanParser, TD-1 retype) check out against the code.

findings.title: Success criteria and verification walkthrough are unsatisfiable as written; several site counts don't reconcile with the code
findings.description:
- The functional requirement (line 135) demands "zero matches in the six swept files," but under TD-3 the 3 `WorkflowNavigator` sites and ~30 raw-string `ConsistencyChecker` sites stay bare — matches necessarily remain. If they are swept instead, the requirement is met but TD-3 is violated (see FAIL above). Either way the criterion as stated can't be satisfied.
- The exclusion filter in the grep (`grep -v 'introspection/types.ts:[3-6]:'`) removes only the `STATUS` definition, but `types.ts:269` (the `SliceStatus.status` union's `'complete'`) and `frontmatterSchema.ts` (lines 32, 34, 257) still match the pattern — so the walkthrough's "After: 4 (types.ts) + frontmatterSchema (3) + SliceStatus.status (4)" bookkeeping (line 149-150) doesn't describe what the command returns. The claimed "8 out-of-scope sites in frontmatterSchema.ts/types.ts SliceStatus" is actually 4 under the given regex (3 frontmatterSchema + 1 types.ts:269).
- Table count errors verified against code: `statusNormalizer.ts`'s `STATUS_MAP` has **14** value-side sites (lines 5-18), not 13; the `types.ts` row's "5 (of 8 total; 4 are the STATUS definition)" doesn't reconcile — actual is 4 (lines 3-6) + 3 (line 44 union) + 1 (line 269) = 8 total, of which 3 are in scope, not 5.
- Minor: the Component Structure table lists 7 files (including `ProjectModelBuilder.ts`, "No change") while the criteria and scope say "six swept files."

findings.title: "Explicitly excluded → Test files" claim ("grep confirms zero .test.ts files assert against these literals") is factually false
findings.description: Direct counterexamples: `packages/core/tests/introspection/taskFileParser.test.ts:48,54,61,73,80` assert `expect(result.inferredStatus).toBe('in-progress' | 'complete' | 'not-started')`; `WorkflowNavigator.test.ts:89` asserts `.toBe('in-progress')`; `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts` builds fixtures with `inferredStatus: 'complete' | 'in-progress' | 'not-started'` (lines 86, 182, 204, 229, 271, 295, 356, 390, 555, 644). The *conclusion* survives by luck — runtime values are unchanged by construction, and the fixture literals remain assignable to the widened `NormalizedStatus` — so no test changes are indeed needed. But the design states a grep was run that returns zero matches when the match count is ~16 lines, which is the same unreliable verification methodology that produced the FAIL finding above.

findings.title: TD-1's stated reason for pairing `types.ts` with `taskFileParser.ts` is technically wrong (though pairing is harmless)
findings.description: The claim that "retyping alone would leave taskFileParser.ts's still-bare-string assignments failing to compile" is incorrect: widening `TaskFileResult['inferredStatus']` to `NormalizedStatus` keeps every existing literal assignment assignable, so the intermediate state builds. Sweeping without retyping also compiles. The steps are genuinely independent; landing them together is still fine for coherence, but the compile-failure justification should be corrected so a future reader doesn't infer a coupling that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Slice is squarely within the maintenance architecture's scope and honors the 241 handoff correctly
findings.description: The work matches architecture 900's Scope bullets ("Pattern consolidation and code quality improvements", "Hard-coded values → configuration or constants") and its principle of themed slices with clear success criteria. The `dependencies: [241]` edge is correct and verified: slice 241 TD-6 explicitly defers the sweep to maintenance slice 910, defines `STATUS` in `introspection/types.ts`, and 910 only consumes it (no changes to `STATUS`). `interfaces: []` / "Provides to Other Slices: None" is right for an internal-representation change — `NormalizedStatus`'s union is unchanged, so CLI/MCP consumers see identical values across the package boundary.

findings.title: Exclusion analysis (TD-2) and supporting factual claims are accurate where verified
findings.description: Verified against code: `frontmatterSchema.ts`'s `VALID_STATUSES` uses underscored raw tokens and includes `deferred` (frontmatterSchema.ts:29-34), which has no `NormalizedStatus` counterpart per `statusNormalizer.ts`'s own doc comment; `STATUS_MAP` keys are raw aliases that must stay literal; `ProjectModelBuilder.ts`'s `'unknown'` sentinel is a TD-2a resolution-failure marker (ProjectModelBuilder.ts:178-181, 250-256), not a `STATUS` value; and `statusDerivation.ts:1` indeed establishes the combined `import { STATUS, type NormalizedStatus }` pattern the design proposes for `statusNormalizer.ts`. The defect is that the sweep table doesn't apply this (correct) vocabulary-split reasoning to `ConsistencyChecker`'s raw-frontmatter sites — see the FAIL finding.

findings.title: Regression strategy satisfies the architecture's "no behavior changes without tests" principle
findings.description: Every swept module has an existing dedicated test file (`taskFileParser.test.ts`, `slicePlanParser.test.ts`, `statusNormalizer.test.ts`, `WorkflowNavigator.test.ts`, `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts`, `types.test.ts`), and the migration plan builds and runs each per step plus a full `pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test` pass with an explicit expected baseline. Since `STATUS.X === 'x'` by construction (verified in `types.ts:3-6` and the derived union), relying on the existing suite as the regression guard is proportionate — no new tests are needed for a zero-behavior-change sweep.
